cohort: 4,386 vertex-presenting singleton newborns with a gestational age of 24-30 weeks and birth weight of 500-1500g, without major congenital malformations, born between 2001 and 2011 at Neocosur centers
finding: Antenatal steroids were associated with improved survival and sIVH-free survival in preterm infants regardless of delivery mode, while the combination of antenatal steroids and cesarean delivery was associated with improved outcomes specifically at 24-25 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: At 24-25 weeks gestation, infants born via cesarean section who received antenatal steroids had higher rates of survival and sIVH-free survival compared to those who received antenatal steroids but were delivered vaginally.
